reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: ServiceRegistry::getFees is used to enforce Smart Escrow limits that are described as being controlled by fee voting, but this implementation returns the startup config (config_->FEES) rather than the currently-active ledger fee settings. That means preflight can validate against stale values until the next fee-setting transaction/ledger update. Consider sourcing these values from the validated/published ledger (e.g., LedgerMaster::getValidatedLedger()->fees()) and falling back to config only when no ledger is available (startup/standalone).

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body:
calculateAdditionalReserve() claims the first 500 bytes are included in the normal reserve, but the current formula `1 + (size / 500)` charges an extra reserve at exactly 500 bytes (and every exact multiple). If the intent is “extra reserve per additional 500 bytes beyond the first”, use a rounding scheme like `1 + ((size - 1) / 500)` (and handle size==0 defensively). If the current behavior is intended, the comment should be corrected to match it.
```suggestion
    return 1 + ((finishFunction->size() - 1) / 500);
```

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body:
The fee rounding for ComputationAllowance currently always adds 1 drop: `(...)/MICRO_DROPS_PER_DROP + 1`. That overcharges by 1 drop when the division is exact (e.g., allowance*gasPrice is already a whole drop). If you need ceiling division, compute it as `(x + denom - 1) / denom` (or add 1 only when there is a non-zero remainder).
```suggestion
        uint64_t const microDropFee =
            (*allowance) * view.fees().gasPrice;
        uint64_t const allowanceFee =
            (microDropFee / MICRO_DROPS_PER_DROP) +
            ((microDropFee % MICRO_DROPS_PER_DROP) != 0 ? 1 : 0);
```

reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body: modifyWasmDataFields takes `beast::Journal viewJ` but doesn't use it. If unused parameters are not consistently suppressed in all build configs, this can trigger warnings. Either remove the parameter, mark it [[maybe_unused]], or use it for trace logging (e.g., when an expected escrow SLE is missing).

3. Alternatively, unify the fee source so both `preflight` and `calculateBaseFee` use the same `Fees` data, eliminating the divergence entirely.

The key principle is: anywhere a gas allowance is accepted, both `gasLimit` and `gasPrice` must be verified as non-zero from the same authoritative source that will be used to compute the actual fee.

## The defect

`gasLimit`, `bytecodeSizeLimit` and `gasPrice` are voted network parameters,
carried in `FeeSettings`. Two paths let a node's own config decide them instead.

`EscrowCreate::preflight` and `EscrowFinish::preflight` read them from
`ServiceRegistry::getFees()`, i.e. this node's `FeeSetup`. So two nodes with
different limits admit different transactions from the same ledger; voting a
limit to `0` disabled nothing; and after activation gas was nearly free, because
`gasPrice` came from the ledger (absent, so `0`) while the guard that would have
refused execution read a non-zero `gasLimit` from config.

Separately, `Ledger::setup` assigned a field only when `FeeSettings` carried it,
leaving an absent one at whatever `fees_` was built with — and every `Ledger` is
built from the local `FeeSetup`. Genesis is the exception: there, reading config
is correct.

## The fix

`preflight` has no view, so it bounds against the protocol ceilings
`kMaxGasLimit` / `kMaxBytecodeSizeLimit`; `preclaim` applies the voted values.
WASM validation moves to `preclaim` too — a cached `preflight` result outlives the
vote that invalidates it — and runs last, since compiling is expensive.

`isBytecodeUploadDisabled` / `isBytecodeExecutionDisabled` are two rungs on
purpose: zeroing `bytecodeSizeLimit` stops new uploads but leaves existing escrows
finishable. Zeroing `gasLimit` stops both.

`Ledger::setup` now resolves an absent field to the protocol constants, amendment
gated; `Change::initializeVMFees` writes them on activation. `getFees()` is
deleted rather than fixed — levelization already forbids `libxrpl` from reaching
config, and this accessor was the way around it.

## Test infrastructure

With `getFees()` gone there is no second fee source to sync.
`TestServiceRegistry` loses `getFees`/`setFees`; `TxTest` gains `setFees(Fees)`,
which writes into `FeeSettings` at the next `close()`.

`FinishFailures.AnAllowancePastTheGasLimitIsRefused` changed meaning: it finished
a nonexistent escrow, fine while the check was in `preflight`. `preclaim` reads
the escrow first and returns `tecNO_TARGET`, so it now creates a real one.

## Notes for reviewers

* `EscrowCreate::preclaim` returns `tem` codes that depend on ledger state.
  Deliberate: these must not claim a fee, and `preflight` cannot see voted values.

prs.body:
## The defect

`gasLimit`, `bytecodeSizeLimit` and `gasPrice` are network parameters: voted, and
carried in the `FeeSettings` ledger object. Two paths let a node's own config
decide them instead.

**Admission read the config file.** `EscrowCreate::preflight` and
`EscrowFinish::preflight` took their limits from `ServiceRegistry::getFees()`,
which returns this node's `FeeSetup`. So:

* **Nodes could disagree.** Two nodes with different limits configured admit
  different sets of transactions from the same ledger.
* **The kill switch did not work.** Voting a limit to `0` writes it to
  `FeeSettings`, which admission never read — so a successful vote to disable
  changed nothing.
* **Gas was nearly free after activation.** The charge is
  `allowance * gasPrice / microDropsPerDrop + 1`, and `gasPrice` came from the
  ledger, where it was absent and read as `0` — one drop for any allowance. The
  guard that would have refused execution read `gasLimit` from config, where it
  was non-zero. One value from each source; either source alone would have been
  safe. Transient: the first fee vote closes it.

**Absent fields inherited the config too.** `Ledger::setup` assigned a field only
when `FeeSettings` carried it, leaving an absent one at whatever `fees_` was
constructed with — and every `Ledger` is built from the local `FeeSetup`. Same
divergence, second route. (Genesis is the exception: there, reading config is
correct.)

## The fix

`preflight` has no view, so it bounds against the protocol ceilings
`kMaxGasLimit` / `kMaxBytecodeSizeLimit`; `preclaim` applies the voted values.

WASM validation moves to `preclaim` too — a cached `preflight` result outlives the
vote that invalidates it — and runs last, since compiling is the expensive step.

`isBytecodeUploadDisabled` / `isBytecodeExecutionDisabled` are two rungs on
purpose: zeroing `bytecodeSizeLimit` stops new uploads but leaves existing escrows
finishable, so the feature can be wound down without forcing holders to wait for
`CancelAfter`. Zeroing `gasLimit` stops both.

`Ledger::setup` now resolves an absent field to the protocol constants, so a
consensus value is either in the ledger or a compile-time constant. Amendment
gated.

`Change::applyAmendment` seeds the three fields on activation; without it they
read as `0` until the first post-activation `SetFee`. That makes the seeded values
consensus-critical, and it is why they are constants rather than `FeeSetup`.

`getFees()` is deleted rather than fixed: levelization already forbids `libxrpl`
from reaching config, and this accessor was the way around it.

## Commits

| | |
|---|---|
| `0d355925a6` | **Fix `FeeSetup::toFees` dropping the extension fee settings.** Pre-existing: it returned only the three base fields, unnoticed because nothing read them yet. The `Fees` constructor now requires every field, so the omission is a compile error. |
| `bc8109388c` | **The divergence fix**, end to end. |
| `5818dad4c1` | **Reduce the defaults** to 400,000 gas / 50,000 bytes. Policy, not part of the fix — separate so it is revertible on its own. |
| `6d14434fb8` | **Floor the voted gas price** at 1,000 micro-drops. `gasPrice` is a price, not a capability, so `0` means free rather than disabled. Enforced at the vote target and the `SetFee`, not at config parse time. |

## Why lower the defaults

Assuming building a ledger has ~1 s execution budget, 200 smart escrow txns running some handcrafted wasm code with 1M gas break this budget. 
Lowering to 400K keeps the execution time way below the budget. 50,000 bytes bounds module compile time, which scales with size and does not charge fuel.

Not restrictive: the largest module in the tree is 10,667 B, so 50 KB leaves
~4.7x headroom on code, and the heaviest contract we can measure
(`all_host_functions`) uses 48,433 gas, so 400K leaves ~8.3x on gas. That gas
figure is a single data point from a contract that calls each host function once
and does not loop, so it is not an upper bound on legitimate usage. Both limits
are voted, so either is one vote from correction.

## Tests

* **`ExtensionFees`** (new gtest) pins the resolution: absent yields the constants
  and *not* the configured values, present still governs, explicit `0` is the kill
  switch rather than absence.
* **`testLimitsIgnoreLocalConfig`** is the regression test — two runs, identical
  genesis, one with a hostile `FeeSetup`; identical results and ledger hash.
* **Kill-switch ladder** covers both rungs, including that zeroing
  `bytecodeSizeLimit` leaves an existing escrow finishable.
* Activation seeding in `FeeVote_test`; `toFees()` round-trip in `Config_test`;
  `gas_price` added to the validations stream test.
* The jtx config stops pinning the three limits — a second source of truth nothing
  read. Tests inherit the defaults and set `[voting]` when they need otherwise.

## Notes for reviewers

* `EscrowCreate::preclaim` returns `tem` codes that depend on ledger state
  (`temTEMP_DISABLED`, `temMALFORMED`). Unusual, but deliberate: these must not
  claim a fee, and `preflight` cannot see the voted values.

The  base, reserve and increment are grandfathered and not amendment-dependent. Genesis writes one representation or the other unconditionally, so those fields are always present in FeeSettings and Ledger::setup always overwrites whatever the Fees was constructed with. Their 0 initializers are never observed.                          
                                                                                                                                                                       
The three extension fields are amendment-dependent: nothing writes them until featureSmartEscrow activates, so there is a real window where the Fees value is what gets used. That is the difference the initializers are tracking.                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                       
Leaving them at 0 is not wrong either, but it has two practical costs. An explicit 0 is the voted kill switch — gasLimit = 0 disables execution, bytecodeSizeLimit = 0 disables uploads — so "not configured yet" and "switched off" become indistinguishable at the point of use. And every test would need to run past a flag ledger and vote before it could do anything, which is a lot of ceremony for a default.                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                       
We also tried the other obvious fix, writing the defaults into genesis FeeSettings unconditionally. That changes the genesis ledger hash and broke a large number of unit tests in unrelated features, so it is not a small change.                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                       
So this is a correct solution that happens to look different from the existing pattern, because the new fields genuinely are in a different position.

## High Level Overview of Change

Adds `GasLimit`, `BytecodeSizeLimit` and `GasPrice` to the network's votable fee
settings, gated on `featureSmartEscrow`. These are the three settings that bound
what a Smart Escrow contract may cost: how much gas one run may burn, how large
a contract may be, and what a unit of gas costs in micro-drops.

Extracted from the `ripple/smart-escrow` feature branch. Replaces the closed #5810.

## Context of Change

`ripple/smart-escrow` is being upstreamed piece by piece. #8157 landed the
`.macro` and autogen plumbing for these fields; this adds the behavior behind
them — config parsing, fee voting, `SetFee`, `FeeSettings` genesis and load, and
the RPC surfaces that report fee settings.

`detail::VotableValue` in `FeeVoteImpl.cpp` becomes a template: it was
hard-wired to `XRPAmount`, and the three new settings are `std::uint32_t`.

`ServiceRegistry::getFees()` exposes the configured settings to code with no
`ReadView` to hand. It has no production caller in this PR; the Smart Escrow
transactors call it from `preflight` in the follow-up. `TestServiceRegistry`
covers it.

`featureSmartEscrow` stays `Supported::No`, so none of this can take effect on a
production network yet.

## API Impact

- [x] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)

Three new response fields, all present only once `featureSmartEscrow` is
enabled: `gas_limit`, `bytecode_size_limit` and `gas_price`, on `server_info`
(`info.validated_ledger`), `subscribe` to `ledger`, and the `validations`
stream. No existing field changes.

## Test Plan

`FeeVote_test` is extended over the three new fields — voting, `SetFee`
application, partial field updates, and config parsing for valid, non-numeric,
negative, overflowing and over-maximum values. `PseudoTx_test` and
`Subscribe_test` run their matrices with and without the amendment.

Full suite on this branch: 248 suites, 4841 cases, 1,280,831 tests, 0 failures.

prs.title: feat: Handle Smart Escrow's Bytecode, Data and Gas fields
prs.author: mvadari
prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds the transaction handling for `EscrowCreate.Bytecode` / `EscrowCreate.Data`
and `EscrowFinish.Gas`, gated on `featureSmartEscrow`: the validation rules, the
fee a contract costs to store, and the owner reserve it occupies.

**Nothing in this PR runs the bytecode.** The WASM engine is not on `develop`,
so `EscrowFinish` stops at a `TODO` where the contract would run and reports
`tecFAILED_PROCESSING`.

Extracted from the `ripple/smart-escrow` feature branch; this is the escrow half
of #6329, which is left holding the WASM engine alone.

Stacked on #8214. Retarget to `develop` once that merges.

## Context of Change

#8157 landed the fields and result codes; #8214 landed the fee settings that
bound a contract. This PR is the transactor behavior: `Bytecode` joins
`FinishAfter` and `Condition` as a way of saying how an escrow completes, priced
at ten base fees plus five drops per byte and reserved at one owner increment
per 500 bytes.

Deliberately absent, so that nothing lands as unreachable code — these arrive
with the WASM engine:

- Screening the module in `preflight` (that it compiles, and imports and exports
  what the engine can serve). Until then any blob of the right size is accepted
  onto the ledger.
- Running the contract, `tecBYTECODE_REJECTED`, and the `Data` a rejected
  contract leaves behind.
- The `GasUsed` and `VMReturnCode` metadata, and the `Transactor` replay path
  that preserves a rejected escrow's `Data`.

`featureSmartEscrow` remains `Supported::No`, so no production network can reach
any of this. The engine PR precedes the `Supported::Yes` flip.

## Before / After

`EscrowCreate`

- `Bytecode` always needs a `CancelAfter`: nothing else can free the funds if
  the contract never accepts.
- `Data` requires `Bytecode`, and is capped at `kMaxWasmDataLength` (1 KB).
- `Bytecode` must be non-empty and within the voted `BytecodeSizeLimit`, and is
  refused with `temTEMP_DISABLED` when fee voting has zeroed `GasLimit` or
  `BytecodeSizeLimit`.
- The owner reserve is one increment per 500 bytes beyond the first 500, on top
  of the increment every escrow costs. `EscrowCancel` and `EscrowFinish` refund
  what was taken.

`EscrowFinish`

- `Gas` is bounded by the voted `GasLimit` and costs `GasPrice` micro-drops
  each, rounded up to the drop.
- `Gas` and the escrow's `Bytecode` must both be present or both absent
  (`tefBYTECODE_NOT_INCLUDED` / `tefNO_BYTECODE`).
- The `tecNO_DST` and deposit-preauth checks move ahead of the condition check,
  so a contract never runs against a destination that cannot receive.

## API Impact

- [x] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)

`EscrowCreate` accepts `Bytecode` and `Data`; `EscrowFinish` accepts `Gas`; the
`Escrow` ledger entry carries `Bytecode` and `Data`. All only once the amendment
is enabled. The fields themselves were added in #8157.

## Test Plan

New `EscrowSmart_test` covers everything that does not need the engine:
amendment gating, every `EscrowCreate` malformity, the fee formula, the reserve
sizing across the 500-byte boundary, insufficient reserve, the on-ledger fields,
the `EscrowFinish` gas bounds and `Bytecode`/`Gas` pairing, fee overflow, and
the reserve refund on cancel. `Escrow_test` gains `- featureSmartEscrow` legs.

Full suite on this branch: 249 suites, 4881 cases, 1,284,994 tests, 0 failures.
